ei.title: A Band United by a Name
ei.subject: 공통영어2

fullPassage: My name is Lee Saem. My first name has an impressive meaning in Korean: “a source of power and vitality.” Since Saem sounds like Sam, I decided to make that my English name. Growing up, I thought Lee was a common last name only in Korea. Little did I know that it’s actually common in many other countries, too. When I searched “Sam Lee” on a social media website, I was amazed at what I saw. There were so many people all over the world with that name! Just for fun, I randomly chose several Sam Lees and sent them friend requests. An Unexpected Connection A lot of them accepted my friend request. While looking through their profiles, I noticed something interesting. Several Sam Lees of various ages and nationalities were interested in music. There was a Sam Lee in his mid-30s from Singapore who enjoyed singing and writing lyrics. And there was a 42-year-old Canadian Sam Lee who was a drummer. According to her profile, everyone called her Sam even though her real name was Samantha. Finally, there was an American Sam Lee who played the electric guitar. Suddenly, I had a great idea. I sent a message to all three. Here is what I wrote: “Hi! I’m Sam Lee from Korea. I write songs and play the keyboard. How about making a virtual band called The Sam Lees?” To my surprise, all three eagerly agreed. That was the start of our band’s journey. The Virtual Music Factory We tried to practice once a week through a video chat app, but we encountered several problems. First of all, we all lived in different time zones. This made it difficult to pick a convenient time for everyone to practice. Secondly, there were audio issues with the app, which caused us to be out of sync. So we put our heads together and devised a better way of playing music. We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in a virtual music factory. After we decided on a song, I would play it on my keyboard and send it to Singaporean Sam. He would sing along with the keyboard and send the recording to American Sam. Then American Sam would add his guitar part, and Samantha would finish the song with her drumming. When it came to choosing songs to play, we took turns. Since each of us prefers a different genre of music and comes from a different culture, we all ended up learning a lot about different kinds of music. It was interesting and a lot of fun. “Long-Distance Friendship” Shortly after we started the band, a global pandemic* began. Since all of our normal lives were put on hold, we valued our online interactions more than ever. At one point, Singaporean Sam became ill and needed to spend some time in the hospital, so the band took a break. However, we still met from time to time by using the video chat app. We talked about our lives and did what we could do to cheer Singaporean Sam up. Since he had to stay in the hospital on his birthday, the rest of us recorded his favorite song as his birthday present. When we played it for him, he laughed so hard that he cried. That was mainly because the song was sung by the worst singer in the band — me! It was good to see him laugh even though he was lying in his hospital bed. After Singaporean Sam recovered, we decided to write and record our own song. We called the song “Long-Distance Friendship,” and we posted it online. The song didn’t get much attention, but we were proud of what we had achieved together. Our band is something really special. Never did we expect that we would build such strong relationships with one another. After all, we don’t come from similar backgrounds, nor have we had the same life experiences. Yet we now talk about almost everything together, including the hardships we face in life. I think it’s been really valuable to get advice from people with such different perspectives. We would all like to meet in person and play our music on the street someday. But even if that never happens, we’ve still been incredibly lucky. Four random people became great friends simply because of our names. Life can be amazing sometimes!

questions.passage: While looking through their profiles, I noticed something interesting.  Several Sam Lees of various ages and nationalities were ①<u>interested</u> in music.  There was a Sam Lee in his mid-30s from Singapore ②<u>who</u> enjoyed singing and ③<u>to write</u> lyrics.  And there was a 42-year-old Canadian Sam Lee who was a drummer.  According to her profile, everyone called her Sam ④<u>even though</u> her real name was Samantha.  Finally, there was an American Sam Lee who played the electric guitar.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ to write → writing: enjoy는 뒤에 -ing(동명사)를 목적어로 쓰고, singing과 짝을 이뤄야 하므로 writing
det.analysis:
① interested: 'were interested in music'은 '음악에 관심이 있었다'라는 뜻이에요. be interested in(~에 관심이 있다)은 늘 이렇게 쓰는 표현이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② who: 'a Sam Lee ~ who enjoyed singing'에서 who는 앞의 사람(a Sam Lee)을 꾸며 주며 '노래하는 것을 즐긴'이라고 이어 주는 관계대명사예요. 사람이 주어 역할을 하니 who가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ to write → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'enjoyed singing and to write lyrics'는 '노래하는 것과 가사 쓰는 것을 즐겼다'예요. 동사 enjoy는 뒤에 반드시 -ing형(동명사)을 써요. 게다가 앞의 singing과 and로 나란히 이어지니(병렬 구조), 같은 -ing 형태인 writing으로 맞춰야 해요. to write는 형태가 달라서 틀려요. ❌ to write는 틀림 ←정답

④ even though: 'even though her real name was Samantha'는 '그녀의 진짜 이름이 Samantha였음에도 불구하고'라는 뜻이에요. even though는 '~에도 불구하고'를 뜻하는 접속사라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: enjoy + 동명사(-ing) / and로 이어지면 앞뒤 형태를 똑같이(singing and writing)

questions.passage: First of all, we all lived in different time zones.  This ①<u>made</u> it difficult to pick a convenient time for everyone to practice.  Secondly, there were audio issues with the app, ②<u>which</u> caused us to be out of sync.  So we put our heads together and devised a better way of ③<u>to play</u> music.  We decided to assemble the songs ④<u>as if</u> we were working in a virtual music factory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ to play → playing: 전치사 of 뒤에는 동명사(-ing)를 써야 하므로 playing
det.analysis:
① made: 'This made it difficult to pick a convenient time'은 '이것은 편한 시간을 고르는 것을 어렵게 만들었다'예요. 여기서 it은 뒤의 to부정사(to pick~)를 대신하는 '가짜 목적어'이고, 진짜 내용은 뒤에 나와요. make + it + 형용사 + to부정사 구조라 made가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② which: 'audio issues with the app, which caused us to be out of sync'는 '앱에 오디오 문제가 있었고, 그것이 우리를 동시에 연주할 수 없게 했다'예요. 콤마 뒤 which는 앞 내용 전체를 받아 '그런데 그것이~'로 이어 주는 계속적 용법이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ to play → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'a better way of to play music'은 '음악을 연주하는 더 나은 방법'이에요. of는 전치사인데, 전치사 뒤에는 반드시 동명사(-ing)를 써야 해요. 그래서 to play가 아니라 playing으로 써야 맞아요. ❌ to play는 틀림 ←정답

④ as if: 'as if we were working in a virtual music factory'는 '마치 우리가 가상의 음악 공장에서 일하는 것처럼'이에요. as if(마치 ~인 것처럼)는 실제가 아닌 상상을 나타낼 때 쓰는 표현이라 맞아요. ✅ 올바름
det.tip: 전치사(of) 뒤에는 동명사(-ing) → a way of playing

questions.passage: Our band is something really special.  ①<u>Never did we</u> expect that we ②<u>would build</u> such strong relationships with one another.  After all, we don’t ③<u>come</u> from similar backgrounds, ④<u>nor we have</u> we had the same life experiences.  Yet we now talk about almost everything together, including the hardships we face in life.  I think it’s been really valuable to get advice from people with such different perspectives.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ nor we have → nor have we: nor로 시작하면 '(조동사)+주어' 순서로 뒤집어야 하므로 nor have we
det.analysis:
① Never did we: 'Never did we expect that~'은 '우리는 ~라고 전혀 예상하지 못했다'예요. Never(부정어)를 문장 맨 앞에 두면 그 뒤를 '조동사(did)+주어(we)' 순서로 뒤집어야 해요(도치). 그래서 Never did we가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

② would build: 'that we would build such strong relationships'는 '우리가 그렇게 끈끈한 관계를 맺게 될 것이라고'예요. 조동사 would 뒤에는 동사원형이 오니 build가 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

③ come: 'we don't come from similar backgrounds'는 '우리는 비슷한 배경 출신이 아니다'예요. don't(do not) 뒤에는 동사원형을 쓰니 come이 맞아요. ✅ 올바름

④ nor we have → 여기가 정답(틀린 곳)! 'nor we have had the same life experiences'는 '~도 아니다'라는 뜻으로 앞의 부정문에 이어져요. nor로 문장을 시작하면 Never처럼 '조동사(have)+주어(we)' 순서로 뒤집어야 해요. 그래서 nor we have가 아니라 nor have we로 써야 맞아요. ❌ nor we have는 틀림 ←정답
det.tip: 부정어(Never/nor)로 시작하면 뒤를 뒤집는다: nor have we

questions.passage: After we decided on a song, I would play it on my keyboard and send it to Singaporean Sam.  He would sing along with the keyboard and send the recording to American Sam.  Then American Sam would add his guitar part, and Samantha would finish the song with her drumming.  When it came to choosing songs to play, we ①<u>took turns</u>.  Since each of us ②<u>prefers</u> a different genre of music and comes from a ③<u>different culture</u>, we all ended up ④<u>forgetting</u> a lot about different kinds of music.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ forgetting → learning: 서로 다른 장르와 문화 덕분에 다른 음악을 '배우게' 되었다는 흐름
det.analysis:
① took turns: 'we took turns'는 '우리는 번갈아 가며 했다'예요. 곡을 고를 때 돌아가며 정했다는 흐름이라 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② prefers: 'each of us prefers a different genre'는 '우리 각자는 서로 다른 장르를 선호한다'예요. 각자 좋아하는 음악이 다르다는 내용이라 맞아요. ✅ 적절

③ different culture: 'comes from a different culture'는 '서로 다른 문화 출신이다'예요. 뒤에 '다른 종류의 음악을 배웠다'로 이어지니 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ forgetting → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'we all ended up learning a lot about different kinds of music'으로 '우리 모두 다른 종류의 음악에 대해 많이 배우게 되었다'예요. 서로 장르와 문화가 다르니 다양한 음악을 '배우게'(learning) 되는 게 자연스러운데, forgetting(잊어버리는)은 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답
det.tip: 다양한 장르·문화 → 서로에게서 배운다(learning), 잊는다(forgetting) 아님

questions.passage: “Long-Distance Friendship” Shortly after we started the band, a global pandemic* ①<u>began</u>.  Since all of our normal lives were put on hold, we valued our online interactions more than ever.  At one point, Singaporean Sam became ②<u>healthy</u> and needed to spend some time in the hospital, so the band took a ③<u>break</u>.  However, we still met from time to time by using the video chat app.  We talked about our lives and did what we could do to cheer Singaporean Sam up.  Since he had to stay in the hospital on his birthday, the rest of us recorded his favorite song as his birthday present.  When we played it for him, he laughed so hard that he ④<u>cried</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② healthy → ill: 병원에 입원해 시간을 보내야 했다는 것은 '아프게(ill)' 되었다는 뜻
det.analysis:
① began: 'a global pandemic began'은 '전 세계적인 유행병이 시작되었다'예요. 밴드 시작 직후에 팬데믹이 시작되었다는 흐름이라 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

② healthy → 여기가 정답(부적절한 곳)! 원문은 'Singaporean Sam became ill and needed to spend some time in the hospital'으로 '싱가포르 Sam이 아프게 되어 병원에서 시간을 보내야 했다'예요. 뒤에 '병원에 입원했다'고 나오니 '아프게(ill)' 된 것이지 '건강해진(healthy)' 것이 아니에요. healthy는 정반대라 문맥에 안 맞아요. ❌ 부적절 ←정답

③ break: 'the band took a break'는 '밴드는 휴식을 취했다'예요. 멤버가 아파서 입원했으니 잠시 쉬는 게 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절

④ cried: 'he laughed so hard that he cried'는 '그는 너무 심하게 웃어서 눈물을 흘렸다'예요. 크게 웃다 보면 눈물이 나기도 하니 자연스러워요. ✅ 적절
det.tip: 병원 입원 → 아프게(ill) 되었다, 건강해진(healthy) 게 아님

questions.passage: This made it difficult to pick a convenient time for everyone to practice.  Secondly, there were audio issues with the app, which caused us to be out of sync.  So we put our heads together and devised a better way of playing music.  We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in __________.  After we decided on a song, I would play it on my keyboard and send it to Singaporean Sam.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① a virtual music factory(가상의 음악 공장): 각자 파트를 하나씩 이어 붙여 노래를 '조립'하는 방식
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in ___'(우리는 마치 ___에서 일하는 것처럼 노래를 조립하기로 했다). 뒤에 각자 키보드→노래→기타→드럼을 차례로 이어 붙이는 과정이 나와요. 공장에서 부품을 하나씩 조립하듯 노래를 만든다는 뜻이라, 빈칸은 '가상의 음악 공장'이 되어야 해요.

✅ ① a virtual music factory(가상의 음악 공장): 온라인으로 파트를 하나씩 이어 붙인다는 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ② a traditional concert hall(전통적인 콘서트홀): 함께 모여 공연하는 곳이라, 각자 떨어져 조립하는 방식과 안 맞아요.

❌ ③ a crowded recording studio(붐비는 녹음실): 한 공간에 모여 녹음하는 이미지라, 서로 다른 나라에 있는 상황과 맞지 않아요.

❌ ④ a professional dance academy(전문 댄스 학원): 춤 이야기는 글에 전혀 없어요.
det.tip: assemble(조립하다) + 파트를 하나씩 이어 붙임 = 음악 '공장(factory)'의 비유

questions.passage: He would sing along with the keyboard and send the recording to American Sam.  Then American Sam would add his guitar part, and Samantha would finish the song with her drumming.  When it came to choosing songs to play, we took turns.  Since each of us prefers a different genre of music and comes from a different culture, we all ended up learning a lot about __________.  It was interesting and a lot of fun.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② different kinds of music(다른 종류의 음악): 각자 다른 장르·문화 출신이라 서로에게서 다양한 음악을 배움
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'Since each of us prefers a different genre of music and comes from a different culture, we all ended up learning a lot about ___'(우리 각자는 서로 다른 장르를 선호하고 다른 문화 출신이기 때문에, 우리 모두는 ___에 대해 많이 배우게 되었다). 서로 좋아하는 장르와 문화가 다르니, 배우게 되는 것은 '다양한 종류의 음악'이 되어야 자연스러워요.

❌ ① the same old songs(늘 똑같은 옛날 노래들): 서로 '다른' 취향이라는 앞 내용과 반대예요.

✅ ② different kinds of music(다른 종류의 음악): 서로 다른 장르·문화 → 다양한 음악을 배운다. 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ how to earn money(돈 버는 법): 돈 이야기는 글에 없어요.

❌ ④ each other's languages(서로의 언어): 언어를 배웠다는 내용은 나오지 않아요.
det.tip: different genre + different culture라는 단서 → different kinds of music

questions.passage: Several Sam Lees of various ages and nationalities were interested in music.  There was a Sam Lee in his mid-30s from Singapore who enjoyed singing and writing lyrics.  And there was a 42-year-old Canadian Sam Lee who was a drummer.  According to her profile, everyone called her Sam even though her real name was Samantha.  Finally, there was an American Sam Lee who played the electric guitar.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ③ 원문 근거: everyone called her Sam even though her real name was Samantha
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문은 싱가포르 Sam이 'enjoyed singing and writing lyrics'(노래와 작사를 즐겼다)이고, 드럼은 캐나다인 Sam이에요. 역할이 바뀌었어요.

❌ ② 원문에서 캐나다인 Sam은 'was a drummer'(드럼 연주자)예요. 전기 기타는 미국인 Sam이 연주했어요. 역할이 바뀌었어요.

✅ ③ 원문 'everyone called her Sam even though her real name was Samantha'(진짜 이름이 Samantha였지만 모두 그녀를 Sam이라 불렀다)와 일치해요. ←정답

❌ ④ 노래와 가사 쓰기를 즐긴 사람은 싱가포르 Sam이에요. 미국인 Sam은 전기 기타를 연주했어요.
det.tip: 인물별 역할: 싱가포르=노래/작사, 캐나다(Samantha)=드럼, 미국=전기 기타

ch: 싱가포르 출신의 Sam Lee는 드럼 연주자였다.
캐나다인 Sam Lee는 전기 기타를 연주했다.
본명이 Samantha인 사람은 모두에게 Sam이라고 불렸다.
미국인 Sam Lee는 노래와 가사 쓰기를 즐겼다.

questions.passage: First of all, we all lived in different time zones.  This made it difficult to pick a convenient time for everyone to practice.  Secondly, there were audio issues with the app, which caused us to be out of sync.  So we put our heads together and devised a better way of playing music.  We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in a virtual music factory.  After we decided on a song, I would play it on my keyboard and send it to Singaporean Sam.  He would sing along with the keyboard and send the recording to American Sam.  Then American Sam would add his guitar part, and Samantha would finish the song with her drumming.  When it came to choosing songs to play, we took turns.  Since each of us prefers a different genre of music and comes from a different culture, we all ended up learning a lot about different kinds of music.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: ① 원문: 영상 채팅 앱으로 연습하려 했고, 오디오 문제로 오히려 동시 연주가 안 됨(직접 만난 것이 아님)
det.analysis:
✅ ① 여기가 정답(일치하지 않는 것)! 원문은 'We tried to practice ~ through a video chat app'(영상 채팅 앱으로 연습하려 했다)이고, 오디오 문제 때문에 'out of sync'(동시에 연주할 수 없었다)라고 했어요. 직접 만나 연습한 것이 아니라 온라인으로 했고, 오디오 문제는 오히려 방해가 되었으니 원문과 반대예요. ←정답

❌ ② 원문 'we all lived in different time zones. This made it difficult to pick a convenient time'과 일치해요.

❌ ③ 원문 'We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in a virtual music factory'와 일치해요.

❌ ④ 원문 'When it came to choosing songs to play, we took turns'와 일치해요.
det.tip: 함정: '직접 만나 연습' → 원문은 영상 채팅 앱(온라인)으로 연습

ch: 밴드는 오디오 문제 때문에 매주 직접 만나서 연습했다.
시간대가 서로 달라 모두에게 편한 연습 시간을 정하기 어려웠다.
그들은 마치 가상의 음악 공장에서처럼 노래를 조합하기로 했다.
연주할 곡을 고를 때 그들은 번갈아 가며 정했다.

questions.passage: “Long-Distance Friendship” Shortly after we started the band, a global pandemic* began.  Since all of our normal lives were put on hold, we valued our online interactions more than ever.  At one point, Singaporean Sam became ill and needed to spend some time in the hospital, so the band took a break.  However, we still met from time to time by using the video chat app.  We talked about our lives and did what we could do to cheer Singaporean Sam up.  Since he had to stay in the hospital on his birthday, the rest of us recorded his favorite song as his birthday present.  When we played it for him, he laughed so hard that he cried.  That was mainly because the song was sung by the worst singer in the band — me!  It was good to see him laugh even though he was lying in his hospital bed.  After Singaporean Sam recovered, we decided to write and record our own song.  We called the song “Long-Distance Friendship,” and we posted it online.  The song didn’t get much attention, but we were proud of what we had achieved together.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문: we valued our online interactions more than ever
det.analysis:
❌ ① 원문은 'the band took a break'(잠시 휴식을 취했다)이고, 이후 Sam이 회복해 다시 곡을 만들었어요. '영원히 그만두었다'는 틀려요.

❌ ② 원문은 'recorded his favorite song as his birthday present'(그가 좋아하는 노래를 녹음해 선물했다)예요. 새로 작곡한 곡이 아니에요.

❌ ③ 원문은 'The song didn't get much attention'(그 노래는 큰 관심을 받지 못했다)이라, 큰 인기를 얻었다는 건 정반대예요.

✅ ④ 원문 'Since all of our normal lives were put on hold, we valued our online interactions more than ever'(평범한 삶이 멈췄기에 온라인 소통을 여느 때보다 소중히 여겼다)와 일치해요. ←정답
det.tip: 핵심: 휴식(영원 아님) / 좋아하는 노래(새 곡 아님) / 큰 관심 못 받음

ch: 싱가포르 Sam이 입원하자 밴드는 활동을 영원히 그만두었다.
그들은 Sam의 생일에 새로 작곡한 곡을 선물로 연주했다.
그들이 만든 노래 Long-Distance Friendship은 온라인에서 큰 인기를 얻었다.
그들은 팬데믹 동안 온라인 소통을 이전보다 더 소중히 여겼다.

questions.passage: Our band is something really special.  Never did we expect that we would build such strong relationships with one another.  After all, we don’t come from similar backgrounds, nor have we had the same life experiences.  Yet we now talk about almost everything together, including the hardships we face in life.  I think it’s been really valuable to get advice from people with such different perspectives.  We would all like to meet in person and play our music on the street someday.  But even if that never happens, we’ve still been incredibly lucky.  Four random people became great friends simply because of our names.  Life can be amazing sometimes!
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② 서로 다른 배경의 네 사람이 같은 이름을 계기로 만나 특별한 우정을 쌓았다는 것이 글 전체의 핵심
det.analysis:
글의 마무리는 '배경도 경험도 다른 우리가 이렇게 끈끈한 관계를 맺게 될 줄 몰랐다', '네 명의 무작위의 사람들이 그저 이름 때문에 좋은 친구가 되었다'예요. 즉 '같은 이름'을 계기로 만난 낯선 사람들이 깊은 우정을 쌓았다는 것이 주제예요.

❌ ① 음악을 배우는 '방법'이 글의 중심이 아니에요. 음악은 이들이 친해진 계기일 뿐이에요.

✅ ② 우연히 같은 이름으로 만난 사람들이 쌓은 특별한 우정: 'Four random people became great friends simply because of our names'와 정확히 통해요. ←정답

❌ ③ 홍보 전략은 글에 나오지 않아요. 오히려 노래는 큰 관심을 받지 못했다고 했어요.

❌ ④ 오해를 피하는 대화 기술을 다루는 글이 아니에요.
det.tip: 핵심 문장: 이름(names) 덕분에 낯선 이들이 great friends가 됨

우연히 같은 이름으로 만난 사람들이 쌓은 특별한 우정
성공적인 온라인 밴드가 되기 위한 홍보 전략

questions.passage: My name is Lee Saem.  My first name has an impressive meaning in Korean: “a source of power and vitality. ” Since Saem sounds like Sam, I decided to make that my English name.  Growing up, I thought Lee was a common last name only in Korea.  Little did I know that it’s actually common in many other countries, too.  When I searched “Sam Lee” on a social media website, I was amazed at what I saw.  There were so many people all over the world with that name!  Just for fun, I randomly chose several Sam Lees and sent them friend requests.  An Unexpected Connection A lot of them accepted my friend request.  While looking through their profiles, I noticed something interesting.  Several Sam Lees of various ages and nationalities were interested in music.  There was a Sam Lee in his mid-30s from Singapore who enjoyed singing and writing lyrics.  And there was a 42-year-old Canadian Sam Lee who was a drummer.  According to her profile, everyone called her Sam even though her real name was Samantha.  Finally, there was an American Sam Lee who played the electric guitar.  Suddenly, I had a great idea.  I sent a message to all three.  Here is what I wrote: “Hi!  I’m Sam Lee from Korea.  I write songs and play the keyboard.  How about making a virtual band called The Sam Lees? ” To my surprise, all three eagerly agreed.  That was the start of our band’s journey.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ① Friends Brought Together by a Shared Name(같은 이름으로 맺어진 친구들)
det.analysis:
글은 'Sam Lee'라는 같은 이름을 검색해 세계 곳곳의 동명이인들을 찾고, 그중 음악을 좋아하는 사람들과 가상의 밴드를 만들어 친구가 되는 이야기예요.

✅ ① Friends Brought Together by a Shared Name(같은 이름으로 맺어진 친구들): 같은 이름이 사람들을 이어 준다는 글 전체를 담은 제목이에요. ←정답

❌ ② The Secret to Becoming a Famous Musician(유명 음악가가 되는 비결): 유명해지는 방법을 다루지 않아요. 오히려 노래는 큰 관심을 받지 못했어요.

❌ ③ How to Choose the Perfect English Name(완벽한 영어 이름 고르는 법): 이름을 고르는 방법이 아니라, 같은 이름을 계기로 만난 이야기예요.

❌ ④ The Difficulties of Learning a New Language(새 언어를 배우는 어려움): 언어 학습의 어려움은 글의 소재가 아니에요.
det.tip: 제목 = 이름(name)이 사람들을 이어 준다는 글 전체의 핵심을 압축

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 put on hold가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ④ temporarily stopped or suspended(일시적으로 멈추거나 보류된)
det.analysis:
밑줄 문장: 'Since all of our normal lives were put on hold, we valued our online interactions more than ever'(우리의 평범한 삶이 모두 ___되었기에, 온라인 소통을 여느 때보다 소중히 여겼다). 팬데믹으로 일상이 잠시 멈춘 상황이라, put on hold는 '일시적으로 멈추다/보류되다'라는 뜻이에요.

❌ ① made far more exciting than usual(평소보다 훨씬 더 신나게 만든): 일상이 멈춰 힘든 상황이라 반대예요.

❌ ② permanently ended without any warning(경고 없이 영구히 끝난): 팬데믹 이후 다시 일상이 돌아오므로 '영구히'는 틀려요.

❌ ③ strictly controlled by the government(정부에 의해 엄격히 통제된): 정부 통제 이야기는 글에 없어요.

✅ ④ temporarily stopped or suspended(일시적으로 멈추거나 보류된): 팬데믹으로 일상이 잠시 멈춘 상황과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

det.korean: ③ 음악에 관심을 보인 세 명의 Sam Lee(싱가포르 가수, 캐나다 드러머, 미국 기타리스트)
det.analysis:

❌ ① 한국의 밴드 멤버들: 이들은 한 나라 밴드가 아니라 여러 나라의 사람들이에요.

✅ ③ 음악에 관심을 보인 세 명의 Sam Lee: 싱가포르 가수·캐나다 드러머·미국 기타리스트 그 세 사람이에요. ←정답

❌ ④ 검색한 이름들: 이름 목록이 아니라 실제 세 사람(인물)을 가리켜요.

questions.passage: First of all, we all lived in different time zones.  This made it difficult to pick a convenient time for everyone to practice.  Secondly, there were audio issues with the app, which caused us to be out of sync.  So we __________ and devised a better way of playing music.  We decided to assemble the songs as if we were working in a virtual music factory.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: ② put our heads together(머리를 맞대다=함께 고민하다): 문제를 함께 해결해 더 나은 방법을 고안함
det.analysis:
빈칸 문장: 'So we ___ and devised a better way of playing music'(그래서 우리는 ___ 음악을 연주하는 더 나은 방법을 고안했다). 앞에서 시간대와 오디오 문제를 겪었고, 뒤에서 '더 나은 방법을 고안했다'고 하니, 빈칸은 함께 힘을 모아 고민했다는 뜻이 되어야 해요.

❌ ① kept our distance from each other(서로 거리를 두었다): 함께 방법을 고안했다는 뒤 내용과 반대예요.

✅ ② put our heads together(머리를 맞대다=함께 고민하다): 문제를 같이 풀어 더 나은 방법을 찾았다는 흐름과 딱 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ gave up the band right away(밴드를 당장 그만두었다): 오히려 방법을 찾아 계속했으므로 반대예요.

❌ ④ blamed one another for it(서로를 탓했다): 협력해 해결책을 만든 흐름과 안 맞아요.
det.tip: put one's heads together = 여럿이 머리를 맞대고 함께 고민하다

ch: kept our distance from each other
gave up the band right away

questions.passage: My name is Lee Saem.  My first name has an impressive meaning in Korean: “a source of power and vitality. ” Since Saem sounds like Sam, __________.  Growing up, I thought Lee was a common last name only in Korea.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"나는 그것을 내 영어 이름으로 만들기로 결정했다." (8단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) decided, English, I, make, my, name, that, to 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 8단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: I decided to make that my English name
det.analysis:
한국어 '나는 ~하기로 결정했다'가 핵심이라 '주어(I) + 동사(decided)'로 시작해요.

decide는 뒤에 to부정사를 목적어로 써요: decided → to make(만들기로).

무엇을 만드는가 하면 'make + that(그것) + my English name(내 영어 이름)'으로 'make A B(A를 B로 만들다)' 구조예요: make → that → my → English → name.

순서대로 놓으면 I / decided / to / make / that / my / English / name → 'I decided to make that my English name'.
det.tip: decide + to부정사 / make A B(A를 B로 만들다): make that my English name

questions.wa: I decided to make that my English name
accept: I decided to make that my English name

questions.passage: We talked about our lives and did what we could do to cheer Singaporean Sam up.  Since he had to stay in the hospital on his birthday, the rest of us recorded his favorite song as his birthday present.  When we played it for him, he laughed so hard that he cried.  That was mainly because the song was ①<u>sang</u> by the worst singer in the band — me!  It was good to see him laugh even though he was lying in his hospital bed.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①은 어법상 틀렸다. 어법에 맞게 올바른 형태로 고쳐 쓰시오. (한 단어, 영어로)

det.korean: sang → sung: 'the song was ___'는 수동태라 be동사 뒤에 과거분사 sung
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'That was mainly because the song was ①<u>sang</u> by the worst singer in the band — me!'예요. '그 노래가 밴드에서 가장 노래를 못하는 나에 의해 불렸기 때문이었다'라는 뜻이에요.

여기서 'the song(노래)'은 부르는 주체가 아니라 '불려지는' 대상이에요. 이렇게 '~되다/~당하다'를 나타낼 때는 수동태 'be동사 + 과거분사(p.p.)'를 써요.

sing의 3단 변화는 sing – sang – sung이에요. sang은 '과거형(불렀다)'이고, 수동태에 필요한 '과거분사'는 sung이에요. 그래서 'was sang'이 아니라 'was sung(불려졌다)'으로 고쳐야 맞아요.

바로 뒤 'by the worst singer(가장 노래 못하는 사람에 의해)'라는 표현도 이 문장이 수동태임을 알려 줘요.
det.tip: 수동태 be + 과거분사: sing–sang–sung 중 과거분사는 sung → was sung

questions.passage: Our band is something really special.  __________ with one another.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"우리는 서로 그렇게 끈끈한 관계를 맺게 되리라고는 전혀 예상하지 못했다." (11단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) build, did, expect, Never, relationships, strong, such, that, we, we, would 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 11단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: Never did we expect that we would build such strong relationships
det.analysis:
핵심은 '전혀 ~하지 못했다'라는 강한 부정이에요. 이럴 때 부정어 Never를 문장 맨 앞에 두면, 그 뒤를 '조동사(did) + 주어(we) + 동사원형(expect)' 순서로 뒤집어요(도치): 'Never did we expect'.

expect 뒤에는 that절(~라는 것을)을 목적어로 붙여요: that + we + would build(맺게 될 것이다).

무엇을 맺느냐 하면 'such strong relationships(그렇게 끈끈한 관계)'예요. such는 '그렇게 ~한'의 뜻으로 형용사(strong) 앞에 놓여요: such → strong → relationships.

순서대로 이으면 Never / did / we / expect / that / we / would / build / such / strong / relationships.
det.tip: 부정어 Never로 시작 → did we expect(도치) / such + 형용사 + 명사

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"우리는 우리의 온라인 소통을 여느 때보다 더 소중히 여겼다."

[ ever / interactions / more / online / our / than / valued / we ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: we valued our online interactions more than ever
det.analysis:
우리말 '우리는 ~을 더 소중히 여겼다'를 영어 어순으로 놓아요.

먼저 주어와 동사: we(우리는) + valued(소중히 여겼다).

무엇을 소중히 여겼는가 하면 목적어 'our online interactions(우리의 온라인 소통)'예요: our → online → interactions.

'여느 때보다 더'는 more than ever라는 굳어진 표현이라 통째로 끝에 붙여요: more → than → ever.

순서대로 이으면 we / valued / our / online / interactions / more / than / ever → 'we valued our online interactions more than ever'.
det.tip: more than ever = 여느 때보다 더(굳어진 표현, 문장 끝)

questions.wa: we valued our online interactions more than ever
accept: we valued our online interactions more than ever

questions.passage: First of all, we all lived in different time zones.  __________ for everyone to practice.
questions.stem:
다음 우리말 뜻에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 모두 배열하여 문장을 완성하시오.

"이것은 편한 시간을 고르는 것을 어렵게 만들었다." (9단어) (영어로) [조건] (1) a, convenient, difficult, it, made, pick, This, time, to 를 모두 사용 (2) 정확히 9단어로 쓸 것

det.korean: This made it difficult to pick a convenient time
det.analysis:
'이것은 ~을 어렵게 만들었다'가 핵심이라 'This(이것은) + made(만들었다)'로 시작해요.

여기서 make는 'make + 목적어 + 형용사(~을 …하게 만들다)' 구조를 써요. 그런데 진짜 목적어(시간을 고르는 것)가 길어서 뒤로 보내고, 그 자리에 '가짜 목적어' it을 먼저 놓아요: made → it → difficult.

뒤로 보낸 진짜 내용은 to부정사로 나타내요: to pick(고르는 것) + a convenient time(편한 시간을). 형용사 convenient가 time을 꾸며요.

순서대로 이으면 This / made / it / difficult / to / pick / a / convenient / time → 'This made it difficult to pick a convenient time'.
det.tip: make it + 형용사 + to부정사: it은 뒤의 to pick~을 대신하는 가목적어

questions.wa: This made it difficult to pick a convenient time
accept: This made it difficult to pick a convenient time
